mood: International Typographic Style: a white field, black grotesque type, one Swiss-red accent, and a grid you can feel. Signatures to reproduce structurally: (1) every page opens with a thick 4px --ink rule across the top of the leaf, with the chapter number set HUGE (10–14rem, weight 800, tight tracking) in --rule gray behind or beside the title — the numeral is a graphic element, not a label; (2) headings are bold, tightly-tracked, sentence case, often flush-left against generous whitespace — asymmetry is the layout tool; (3) accents are used with extreme discipline: red appears only on links, key terms, and one pull-quote rule per page. No shadows, no rounded corners beyond 2px, no gradients on components, no decoration that isn't information. Diagrams are thin-stroke, labeled in small caps. The feel: Müller-Brockmann designing a systems textbook — rational, confident, quietly beautiful.
